chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from the one who narrated to him, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the price of what is in the turtle dove, the laughing dove, the quail, the sparrow, and the nightingale. So he (peace be upon him) said: Its price is [one price]. But if he catches it while he is in Ihram in the Haram, then [the penalty is] two prices, and there is no blood [sacrifice] upon him regarding it.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for catching birds while in Ihram inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific financial compensation (qimah) for catching wild birds like the turtle dove and sparrow while in Ihram within the Haram boundaries, establishing a double-value penalty without requiring a blood sacrifice (dam). It reflects the Shia juristic distinction between the penalty for hunting in the sacred precincts versus general hunting restrictions, emphasizing that the severity of location (Haram) dictates the financial multiplier rather than the type of animal. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for determining the precise valuation of game in cases of Ihram violations.
